name: Shaphan
description: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Hilkiah the high priest finds the book of the law in the house of the Most High and gives it to Shaphan, who reads it. Manasseh and Amon were so wicked the very book of the law had been lost.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

points: Shaphan reports to the king about the money and the workmen, then tells him Hilkiah delivered him a book, and reads it before the king.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

points: Over the people left in the land Nebuchadnezzar made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: In the eighteenth year of his reign, when he has purged the land and the house, Josiah sends Shaphan, Maaseiah, and Joah to repair the house of the Lord his God.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

points: Shaphan carries the book to the king and reads it before him, reporting that all committed to the servants is being done and the money delivered to the workmen.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

points: When the king hears the words of the law, he rends his clothes and commands Hilkiah, Ahikam, Abdon, Shaphan, and Asaiah to go inquire of the Lord for him and for the remnant left in Israel and Judah.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

points: One king knew the word came from the Most High and spared the prophet, while another king put his prophet to death; nevertheless the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah so he was not given to the people to be killed.
